title: Tavelo Grow – Watch Before You Buy!

takeaways.text: First shown in January 2026, the frame took over half a year to reach regular customers.

The seat angle is slack and gets slacker on larger sizes, so even the zero-offset post limits a forward race position; Tavelo insisted the post supplied as zero-offset was correct, which the presenter doubted.
The seatpost went in only about 120 mm rather than the 150 mm maximum listed for size S, leaving about 10 mm of adjustment once cut.
Size S: frame 987 g, fork 464 g, seatpost 182 g, headset 80 g, axles 57 g and small parts 26 g, 1,796 g in total; the tubes feel sturdy rather than thin.

The headset bearing seats showed filler rework and the bearings sat very loosely before compression; the threaded BSA shell and brake mounts were clean. The drain hole is tiny and not at the lowest point.

1× only with no front-derailleur mount; flat-mount fork for 140 or 160 mm rotors (no 180 mm option); FIDLOCK storage with a well-sealed lid and a 19 g internal divider bolt; clearance 55 mm front and 50 mm rear per Tavelo.

disclosure: Inspection of a teammate's size S frameset ordered through Panda Podium, a retailer that sells Tavelo; the presenter rides a competing Quick Pro frame.
summary: Detailed frameset inspection of a size S Tavelo Grow: weights, seatpost fit, bearing seats, routing and storage.
